newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU floated daily refund scheme for oats - sources.
newsitem.headline: EU floated daily refund scheme for oats - sources.

text.p: The European Union considered introducing a daily export refund for Scandinavian oats this week but withdrew the proposal because of legal difficulties, EU member-country sources said on Friday.

The EU has commitments to offer oats onto the world market under accession arrangements with Finland and Sweden, which joined the bloc last year. But Brussels has so far rejected exporters' subsidy bids of over 30 Ecus a tonne as too high.
The idea of a flat "common right" refund for oats was floated by the European Commission at an EU cereals management committee in Brussels on Thursday, a committee source said.
Sources said the Commission's ideas on a level for the refund appeared to be close to the 30 Ecus mark, less than the amount traders sought at the same day's weekly tender.
Common right refunds are allocated on a first-come first-served basis through a daily channel, rather than the variable refunds available by tender through the weekly system.
The committee source said the idea of a fixed daily refund had been dropped during discussions because it could not legally be restricted to two exporters, Finland and Sweden.

Export of oats is a sensitive issue for Scandinavian farmers but which has broader reach because the main importer is the United States -- the EU's main export rival for other grains and hardly a traditional beneficiary of EU subsidies, traders at an industry gathering said.
Traders on Thursday placed eight weekly bids for oat export refunds, covering 113,000 tonnes, at levels between 33.49 and 39.25 Ecus per tonne, industry sources said. Bids were rejected.

One source said the informal discussion of a daily refund of some 30 Ecus per tonne had at least given the market a signal that similar bids at the weekly auction had a better chance of being accepted.
"I think if they had bid 30 (the EU) would have given it," the source said.
